lesson.title: Je voudrais
lesson.subtitle: vouloir, pouvoir, faire in the conditional (je voudrais, tu pourrais, je ferais).

hook.title: Climbing the Politeness Escalator with je voudrais and tu pourrais
hook.content: Replace blunt Je veux ('I want') with conditional Je voudrais ('I would like') and Tu pourrais ('Could you') whenever ordering or asking a favor!

footnotes.title: Why je voudrais and tu voudrais sound identical (/vudʁɛ/)
footnotes.content: Because the conditional uses the -ais, -ais, -ait endings of the imparfait, je voudrais, tu voudrais, and il/elle/on voudrait all sound like /vudʁɛ/!

pattern.title: Je voudrais + Noun OR Bare Infinitive
pattern.content: Use Je voudrais before a noun (Je voudrais l'addition) or before a bare infinitive (Je voudrais réserver une table).
pattern.linguist_note: Conditional mood attenuates directive speech acts by framing desires politely.
pattern.trap_note: Never insert à or de after je voudrais before an infinitive — chain the infinitive bare: Je voudrais partir!

exercises.prompt: Match each conditional request with its English meaning:

matching_pairs.english: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît
matching_pairs.german: I would like a coffee, please
I would like the bill / check

matching_pairs.english: Je voudrais vous demander quelque chose
matching_pairs.german: I would like to ask you something

exercises.target_answer: I would like a coffee, please, I would like the bill / check, I would like to ask you something, Could you help me?, We would like two tickets
exercises.meaning: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît, Je voudrais l'addition, Je voudrais vous demander quelque chose, Tu pourrais m'aider ?, On voudrait deux billets
exercises.explanation: voudrais / voudrait and pourrais turn blunt demands into warm courtesy.

exercises.prompt: You want to ask the waiter for the bill (l'addition). Which phrasing is most polite and natural?
options: Je voudrais l'addition, s'il vous plaît
exercises.target_answer: Je voudrais l'addition, s'il vous plaît
exercises.meaning: I would like the bill, please
exercises.explanation: Je voudrais is the universal polite standard in restaurants and shops.

exercises.prompt: Soften 'Je veux voir le directeur' ('I want to see the director') using the conditional of vouloir:
exercises.meaning: I would like to see the director

exercises.idea: could you come with me today (informal tu)
cues: You could come → Tu pourrais venir
with me today → avec moi aujourd'hui
exercises.target_answer: Tu pourrais venir avec moi aujourd'hui
exercises.meaning: Could you come with me today?

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Nous voudrions réserver une table pour quatre personnes
exercises.target_answer: Nous voudrions réserver une table pour quatre personnes
exercises.meaning: We would like to reserve a table for four people
exercises.affirmation: You wrote Nous voudrions réserver and quatre personnes cleanly.

summary.outcome: Use je voudrais, on voudrait, and tu pourrais to order and make polite requests.

use_example.german: Bonjour, je voudrais deux billets pour Lyon, s'il vous plaît.
use_example.english: Hello, I would like two tickets to Lyon, please.

summary.takeaway: Swap je veux for je voudrais whenever you order or ask a favor.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([2602] The -ai Future): see how Je voudrais leads directly into The -ai Future.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "Could you come with me today" in French:
twist.target_answer: Tu pourrais venir avec moi aujourd'hui
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Tu pourrais venir avec moi aujourd'hui" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of Je voudrais.

voudrais.context_phrase: Je voudrais un croissant, s'il vous plaît.
voudrais.context_translation: I would like a croissant, please.
voudrais.etymology_derivation: Future stem voudr- + imparfait ending -ais = the polite conditional!

vouloir.etymology_derivation: Latin volō 'I want' → vouloir. A volunteer is the one who wants to do — the want-root English kept in voluntary, benevolent.

sil_vous_plait.etymology_derivation: 'if it pleases you' — politeness as a small conditional; compare 'if you please', which English still owns.

table.etymology_derivation: Latin tabula 'board, plank'. English borrowed the French word whole — remember it is feminine: la table.

café.etymology_derivation: Turkish kahve → Italian caffè → French café. English took the same journey twice: coffee and café.

vin.context_translation: I would like some red wine.

addition.etymology_derivation: The restaurant bill is literally 'the addition' of the prices.
